unique_issues: IMSE bandwidth 0.22 on vote share is far too wide for a close-election RD (3x the scalar RD's 0.08), undermining identification.
The proof that the quantile-treatment cross-covariance sigma_12=0 is a vacuous algebraic cancellation; fuzzy-design covariance may be misspecified.
Fuzzy 'monotonicity' I5 forces all near-cutoff units to be compliers, far stronger than standard no-defiers; mislabeled as standard.
Calling Q-RD 'biased and inconsistent' is a category error: it consistently estimates a different (pooled-mixture) estimand, not the barycenter.
Matching outcomes to the governor's final tenure year (~3-year lag, state-specific offset) lets common macro shocks confound the RD; not addressed.

weak_or_unjustified.why: A design-specific IMSE bandwidth being ~3x a different (scalar) design's bandwidth is normal; the leap to 'undermines identification' is unjustified.
The displayed sigma_12 step is a correct algebraic cancellation; branding it 'vacuous' and inferring fuzzy misspecification overstates a corroborated point.

unique_issues: The proof that the quantile-treatment covariance sigma_12 equals zero is a vacuous identity and is false for the fuzzy design, affecting F3D variance.
The identity-derivative argument for Fréchet inference requires strict monotonicity (L4), which plausibly fails at low income quantiles, invalidating the bottom-quantile bands.
Calling Q-RD 'biased and inconsistent' overclaims: it is consistent for a different estimand; the issue is target mismatch, not lack of consistency.

weak_or_unjustified.why: Asserts L4 fails specifically at low income quantiles without evidence on the density there; the failure region is claimed, not shown.

unique_issues: The proof that cross-covariance sigma_12 = 0 is invalid for the fuzzy design; it omits the joint moment E[Q_Y(q)T|x], so the fuzzy-Wald variance is wrong.
Table 2 coverage/homogeneity acceptance is byte-identical across all Delta values within each n, statistically implausible and suggesting a tabulation/coding bug.
Lemma 2's 'no-regret in all L_p including L_infinity' does not follow generically from an L^2 projection and the per-x indexing is a notational error.
The Proposition A-3 derivation equates an L2-squared distance to an un-squared W_2 distance and has sign errors, leaving the core Frechet equivalence unproven as written.
Calling the DGP1 treatment effect 'closed-form N(Delta,2)' conflates a constant scalar effect tau(q)=Delta with a distribution; the variance '2' is unexplained.

weak_or_unjustified.why: Likely misreads notation: N(Delta,2) almost certainly specifies the outcome DGP (mean shift Delta, variance 2), not a claim that the treatment effect itself is a distribution.
Asserts 'sign errors' in Proposition A-3 without exhibiting them; the L2-squared-vs-W2 point may be real but the claim is stated, not demonstrated.

verdict: The non-English conditions did not collapse: all three recovered the same five strongest English problems (winsorizing/L4, asymptotic-equivalence-vs-superiority, i.i.d. state-years/clustering, the Q1 small-group rate, and the barycenter-not-causal LAQTE), and several surfaced legitimate issues English missed entirely (the sigma_12 fuzzy-covariance proof and the byte-identical Table 2 entries each appear in all three non-English reviews). Recall on the 12 English issues is uneven but not degraded in depth: Chinese is strongest at 0.75 and tracks English most closely, Arabic is 0.67 and trades English's empirical/specification-search concerns (no manipulation test, the 2010 cutoff) for deeper formal proof-level critiques (Lemma 2, Proposition A-3), while Spanish is weakest at 0.50, missing more core items and carrying the shakiest unique claims. The one mild sign of language-specific degradation is Spanish: it has the lowest recall and its two least-justified issues (bandwidth-too-wide 'undermines identification' and the 'vacuous' covariance framing) are weaker than anything in the Chinese review, though no language shows outright fabrication.
